# 07 — Building With Parts (standards, BuildKit, props catalog)

**Read this before building anything.** Every map, prop, character, Frame and Titan is generated by **builder code** (build-as-code) that lives in the local `builders/` folder and is run in Studio through the MCP. This makes every build **reproducible** (rebuild anytime), **tweakable** (change a number, rebuild) and **reviewable** (it's text).

---

## 1. Build-as-code workflow

```
builders/
  lib/BuildKit/              -- primitives and helpers (§3): init.lua + Core, Structure, Detail, Fx, Gameplay (D-009)
  lib/Palette.lua            -- every hex from 06_art_direction.md as Color3 constants
  lib/Props/                 -- prop factory functions (§6): init.lua + Furniture, Display (D-100)
  checks/<Name>              -- spec checks and self-tests (§8); mirrored as DevTools.Checks.<Name> (D-013)
  characters/CharacterKit.lua, characters/<Name>.lua
  rigs/Vanguard.lua, rigs/Strider.lua, rigs/Watcher.lua
  maps/central_command/<Area>.lua    -- one file per area (OpsHall, Quarters, ...)
  maps/hangar/<Area>.lua
  maps/outpost07/<Area>.lua
  maps/backdrops/<Area>.lua
  maps/memory_set.lua
```

- In Studio, mirror these as **ModuleScripts** under `ServerStorage.DevTools` (`DevTools.BuildKit`, `DevTools.Palette`, `DevTools.Props`, `DevTools.Builders.<Folder>.<Name>`). Push them from the local files the same way as game code. `DevTools.Props` returns a function of BuildKit: `local Props = require(DT.Props:Clone())(BK)`; area builders get it injected as `opts.Props` (structure pass and up).
- **Run a builder** through the MCP run-code tool:
  ```lua
  local DT = game:GetService("ServerStorage").DevTools
  -- Clone before require so edited modules aren't served from require's cache
  local builder = require(DT.Builders.CentralCommand.OpsHall:Clone())
  return builder.Build({ pass = "structure" })
  ```
  Inside builders, require BuildKit, Palette and Props the same way (clone, then require), or have the runner inject them: `builder.Build({ BK = BK, P = Palette, Props = Props, pass = ... })`. **Use the injection pattern** (simpler and cache-safe).
- **Every builder must be idempotent:** it finds its target folder (e.g. `Workspace.Map.CentralCommand.OpsHall`), destroys its children, and rebuilds. It never touches anything outside its target.
- **Deterministic:** randomness only through `BK.rng(seed)` with a fixed seed per builder.
- **Return stats:** `{ parts = n, lights = n, ms = elapsedMs, warnings = {...} }`. Claude reports these in the journal.
- **Large builders:** keep each builder file under ~800 lines. Split areas (e.g. `Hangar_Shell`, `Hangar_Bays`, `Hangar_Props`).
- `ServerStorage.DevTools` stays in the place (it's harmless at runtime: ServerStorage isn't replicated). It must never be required by game code.

## 2. Build passes (detail levels)

Each builder supports `opts.pass`:

| Pass | Contents | When |
|---|---|---|
| `blockout` | Correct dimensions, walls, floors, openings, stairs, collisions, spawn points, triggers, nav nodes. Flat palette colors. No props. | Phase 1 (hub), Phase 4 (outpost) |
| `structure` | Blockout plus final materials, trims, windows, doors, columns, ceilings, light fixtures with lights, signage | Phases 1–4 for areas being played |
| `dressed` | Structure plus every prop in the spec, greebles, decals, ambient NPC spots, VFX emitters, panel seams | Phase 7 (and hero areas earlier when listed in the roadmap) |

A higher pass **includes** all lower passes. Gameplay objects (triggers, prompts, pads, spawns, nav nodes) are built in **every** pass so gameplay can be tested on blockouts.

## 3. BuildKit API (implement exactly; extend if needed and document additions here)

```lua
-- builders/lib/BuildKit/ (init.lua + child modules; in Studio: DevTools.BuildKit)
local BK = {}

-- Containers
BK.folder(parent: Instance, name: string, clear: boolean?) -> Folder
BK.model(parent: Instance, name: string) -> Model

-- Primitives (props table keys listed below)
BK.part(parent, props) -> Part
BK.wedge(parent, props) -> WedgePart
BK.cornerWedge(parent, props) -> CornerWedgePart
BK.cyl(parent, props) -> Part   -- Shape=Cylinder; props.Axis = "X"|"Y"|"Z" orients the cylinder's length
BK.ball(parent, props) -> Part
BK.truss(parent, props) -> TrussPart

-- Spec-friendly builders (coordinates straight from the map docs)
BK.box(parent, name, min: Vector3, max: Vector3, props) -> Part         -- axis-aligned box from corners
BK.floor(parent, name, x1, x2, z1, z2, yTop, thickness, props) -> Part  -- top surface at yTop
BK.ceiling(parent, name, x1, x2, z1, z2, yBottom, thickness, props) -> Part
BK.wallX(parent, name, x1, x2, zCenter, y1, y2, thickness, props) -> Part   -- wall running along X
BK.wallZ(parent, name, z1, z2, xCenter, y1, y2, thickness, props) -> Part   -- wall running along Z
BK.wallWithOpenings(parent, name, axis: "X"|"Z", a1, a2, center, y1, y2, thickness,
    openings: {{from: number, to: number, y1: number, y2: number}}, props) -> Model
    -- splits into segments plus lintels above openings; adds 0.4-stud door-frame trim (STEEL_DARK)
BK.stairs(parent, name, bottomFrontCenter: Vector3, dir: Vector3, width, totalRise,
    opts {stepRise=1, stepRun=1.5, railings=true, stringers=true, material, color}) -> Model
    -- dir is a horizontal unit vector (uphill direction); adds an invisible smooth ramp collider
BK.railing(parent, name, points: {Vector3}, opts {height=3.5, postSpacing=5, color}) -> Model
BK.column(parent, name, baseCenter: Vector3, height, width, opts {capital=true, base=true, color}) -> Model
BK.window(parent, name, cframe, width, height, opts {mullions=2, frameColor}) -> Model
BK.door(parent, name, cframe, width, height, opts {double=false, color, sign}) -> Model

-- Detailing
BK.seams(face: Part, faceEnum: Enum.NormalId, spacing: number, opts {depth=0.1, width=0.2, color}) -> Folder
BK.trimBand(parent, name, cframe, length, height, depth, color) -> Part
BK.kickplate(parent, name, wallPart: Part, side: Enum.NormalId) -> Part      -- 1-stud dark base strip
BK.hazardStripe(parent, name, cframe, length, width, opts {stripe=2, angle=45}) -> Model
BK.pipeRun(parent, name, points: {Vector3}, radius, opts {color, brackets=true}) -> Model
BK.cable(parent, name, a: Vector3, b: Vector3, sag: number, segments: number, thickness) -> Model
BK.bolts(face: Part, faceEnum, grid: Vector2, opts {size=0.3, color}) -> Folder

-- Lights, text, effects
BK.light(onPart: Part, kind: "Point"|"Spot"|"Surface", props) -> Light
BK.sign(parent, name, cframe, size: Vector2, text, opts {font, textColor, bgColor, bgTransparency=0, light=false}) -> Part
BK.screen(parent, name, cframe, size: Vector2, opts {text, color}) -> Part     -- Neon base plus SurfaceGui, LightInfluence 0
BK.emitter(onPart: Part, presetName: string) -> ParticleEmitter                -- presets from 06 §6

-- Gameplay objects (built in every pass)
BK.trigger(parent, name, min: Vector3, max: Vector3, id: string) -> Part      -- invisible, CanCollide false, CanTouch true, tag "Trigger", attribute TriggerId
BK.prompt(onPart: Part, id: string, actionText, opts {hold=0, dist=8, frameOnly=false, onFootOnly=false}) -> ProximityPrompt
    -- tag "Interactable" on the part; attributes InteractId, FrameOnly, OnFootOnly
BK.spawnPoint(parent, id: string, cframe) -> Part       -- invisible marker, tag "SpawnPoint", attribute SpawnId
BK.camPoint(parent, id: string, pos: Vector3, lookAt: Vector3) -> Part    -- tag "CinematicCam", attribute CamId
BK.navNode(parent, id: string, pos: Vector3, links: {string}) -> Part      -- tag "NavNode"
BK.dismountPad(parent, id: string, center: Vector3, radius, exitPoint: CFrame) -> Model  -- tag "DismountPad"
BK.barrier(parent, name, min, max, group: "FrameBarrier"|"PlayerBarrier") -> Part        -- invisible collider

-- Utilities
BK.weld(a: BasePart, b: BasePart) -> WeldConstraint
BK.weldAllTo(model: Model, root: BasePart)
BK.tag(inst, ...: string)
BK.attr(inst, table)
BK.rng(seed: number) -> {next: (min, max) -> number, int: (min, max) -> number, pick: (list) -> any}
BK.vary(color: Color3, amount: number, rng) -> Color3   -- ±brightness variance (amount 0.03 = 3%)
BK.stats(root: Instance) -> {parts, lights, emitters, guis}
BK.hex(hex: string) -> Color3
```

**`props` table keys** (for every primitive): `Name, Size, CFrame | Position (+ Orientation in degrees), Color (Color3 or hex string), Material (Enum or string), Transparency, Reflectance, Anchored (default true), CanCollide (default true), CanQuery (default true), CanTouch (default false), CastShadow (default true), Massless, Locked, Tags, Attributes, CollisionGroup`.

**Defaults that BuildKit applies automatically:**
- `Anchored = true`, `CanTouch = false`, `TopSurface/BottomSurface = Smooth`.
- If every dimension is ≤ 0.5: `CastShadow = false`, `CanCollide = false`, `CanQuery = false`.
- If a part is tagged `Detail`: `CanCollide = false`, `CanQuery = false`.

### 3.1 Additions and conventions (implemented in Phase 0; decisions D-009 to D-013, D-017)

Everything in §3 is implemented with the signatures above. What follows was added or pinned down while implementing it. The self-test `DevTools.Checks.BuildKitCheck` (29 cases) covers all of it; re-run it after any change to `builders/lib/`.

**Loading.** `local BK = require(DevTools.BuildKit:Clone())`. The clone carries its child modules, so the clone-then-require rule still holds. `BK.Palette` is the palette (`BK` loads `DevTools.Palette` itself), so builders can use `local P = BK.Palette`.

**Props rules.** Explicit props always win over the automatic defaults. An unknown props key is an error (it catches typos). Defaults when omitted: `Material = SmoothPlastic`, `Color = CONCRETE_MID`. `Tags` may be a list or a single string.

**Facing and `cframe` conventions.** Everything faces −Z (its LookVector), like props.

| Function | `cframe` / position means |
|---|---|
| `BK.window`, `BK.door` | **Bottom-center** of the opening, on the wall centerline |
| `BK.sign`, `BK.screen`, `BK.trimBand` | **Center** of the part; the readable side of a sign or screen is its Front (−Z) face |
| `BK.hazardStripe` | Center of the band **on the surface**: length along X, width along Z, surface normal along Y |
| `BK.floorText`, `BK.dismountPad` (`center`) | A point **on** the floor |
| `BK.spawnPoint` | Exactly the registry CFrame (on the floor, facing along −Z) |

**Extra functions.**

```lua
BK.beam(parent, name, a: Vector3, b: Vector3, sizeX, sizeY, props) -> Part   -- a box running from a to b
BK.triangle(parent, name, corner: Vector3, legA: Vector3, legB: Vector3, thickness, props) -> WedgePart
    -- right-triangle prism; the right angle is at `corner`, legA and legB are the two perpendicular edges
BK.lookAlong(position: Vector3, direction: Vector3) -> CFrame   -- LookVector along direction; safe when vertical
BK.floorText(parent, name, position: Vector3, size: Vector2, text, opts {textUp = -Z, ...sign opts}) -> Part
    -- painted floor text (06 §7): flat, 0.05 above the floor, HAZARD_YELLOW at 0.15 transparency
BK.darken(color, amount) -> Color3          -- amount 0.08 = 8% darker (seams)
BK.toColor(Color3 | "#RRGGBB") -> Color3
BK.toMaterial(Enum.Material | string) -> Enum.Material
BK.report(root, startClock) -> stats        -- BK.stats + ms + warnings: the table every builder returns
BK.warn(message)                             -- collected in BK.warnings and printed
BK.breathe(force: boolean?)                  -- yields one frame when BK.yieldBudget (default 0.1 s) is used up
BK.emitterPresets                            -- list of preset names for BK.emitter
```

**Glow calibration (D-099).** `BK.GLOW.amber` (`WARNING_ORANGE`, Neon, transparency 0.4) and `BK.GLOW.holo` (the same at 0.6; hologram planes 0.8, edges 0.45) are how a part that should *glow amber* is drawn: Neon brightens colors, and `AMBER` in Neon shows on screen as lemon yellow, while these show as the doc's amber. Door status strips and dismount-pad lamps use it. Light objects keep `AMBER`; amber paint, text and UI stay `AMBER`.

`BK.stats` also returns `shadowLights`. Colors from `BK.darken` and `BK.vary` are snapped to 8 bits per channel, because parts truncate anything finer.

**Large builds.** Studio freezes while edit-mode code runs. BuildKit yields automatically for one frame whenever it has been creating parts for longer than `BK.yieldBudget` seconds (set it to 0 to never yield). Measured: 4,000 parts build in about 60 ms.

**Per-function details and extra options.**

| Function | Behavior and extra options |
|---|---|
| `BK.cyl` | Without `Axis`: the raw engine cylinder (length along local X). With `Axis`: `Size` and `CFrame`/`Position`/`Orientation` describe a logical box whose length runs along that axis, e.g. a standing barrel is `{Axis = "Y", Size = (2.6, 3.6, 2.6)}` |
| `BK.wallWithOpenings` | The trim **replaces** wall material around each opening, so the clear opening keeps exactly the size given (a 5 × 8 doorway stays 5 × 8) and no faces overlap. The trim stands 0.1 proud of both wall faces. `props.Trim = false` or `opening.trim = false` skips it; `props.TrimColor` overrides the color. Parts: `<name>_Seg<n>`, `_Lintel<i>`, `_Sill<i>`, `_Trim<i>_L/_R/_Head/_Sill`. Model attributes: `Openings`, `Axis`, `Opening<i>_Span`, `Opening<i>_Y` (for the door-size check). Openings that overlap or sit closer together than the trim are an error |
| `BK.stairs` | `bottomFrontCenter` is the floor point at the foot of the first riser; the top of the last step is level with the upper floor. The invisible ramp collider (`<name>_RampCollider`, 1 thick, tag `NoCollideCamera`) runs through every step nosing and starts on the floor **one tread before** the first riser. Stringers are two beams under the treads. Railings use `BK.railing` with posts sunk into the treads |
| `BK.railing` | Top rail, mid rail and posts never collide; one invisible collider panel per segment does (`<name>_Collider<i>`, tag `NoCollideCamera`). Extra opts: `sink` (posts and collider reach this far below the base points), `collide = false` |
| `BK.column` | `height` is the total height including base and capital (each 1 tall, 0.5 overhang). Extra opt: `material` |
| `BK.window` | Frame bars 0.4, glass `GLASS` at 0.55 transparency, `mullions` vertical bars. Extra opt: `depth` |
| `BK.door` | Leaf (or two with `double`), a handle, and a Neon status strip above the frame on both wall faces (`AMBER`, or `DANGER_RED` when `locked`). Tagged `Door`; attributes `Locked`, `Width`, `Height`. Extra opts: `leaf = false` (open passage: strips and sign only), `locked`, `wallThickness` (default 1) |
| `BK.seams` | `opts.along` = local axis the lines run along (default: both in-plane axes, a grid); `opts.at` = extra lines at offsets from the face's minimum edge (e.g. `{3, 10}` for the wainscot lines); `opts.align` = `"world"` (default: lines sit on world multiples of the spacing, so neighbouring parts line up), `"center"` or `"edge"`; `opts.parent`, `opts.name` for the returned Folder (default: next to the part) |
| `BK.kickplate` | Optional 5th argument `opts {color, height = 1, depth = 0.1}`. Default color `KICKPLATE`; exterior walls pass `CONCRETE_DARK` |
| `BK.hazardStripe` | Yellow base strip plus black stripes made of flat triangles and rectangles; nothing pokes outside the band. `opts.angle` 15–90 |
| `BK.pipeRun` | Ball elbows at corners, clamp brackets about every 8 studs. Decoration by default; `opts.collide = true` makes it solid |
| `BK.cable` | Optional 8th argument `opts {color}` (default `HAZARD_BLACK`) |
| `BK.bolts` | `grid` = Vector2(columns, rows). Extra opts: `margin`, `parent`, `name` |
| `BK.light` | `props`: `Name, Color (default LIGHT_NEUTRAL), Brightness, Range, Angle, Face, Shadows (default false), Enabled, Tags, Attributes`. `Range` above 60 is clamped with a warning |
| `BK.sign` | Text is forced to ALL CAPS unless `opts.upper = false`. Defaults: amber Michroma on `SLATE_DEEP`. Extra opts: `textTransparency`, `pixelsPerStud` |
| `BK.screen` | `opts.color` is the base color (default `#1B2A33`, transparency 0.3). Extra opts: `textColor`, `font` (default RobotoMono), `transparency`, `pixelsPerStud` |
| `BK.emitter` | Presets from `06` §6: `Sparks`, `Smoke`, `DustPuffOutdoor`, `DustPuffHangar`, `AshFlakes`, `TitanRegen`. Burst presets are created disabled with an `EmitCount` attribute. To be unified with `Shared/Modules/VFX` when that module is written (Phase 2) |
| `BK.prompt` | `Style = Custom`. `frameOnly` prompts default to distance 70 (D-068: measured from the seated pilot, 48.6 studs up) and no line-of-sight check. Extra opts: `once`, `enabled`, `lineOfSight`, `objectText`. The part also gets the `Once` attribute (`13` §4) |
| `BK.camPoint` | Also sets the attribute `LookAt` |
| `BK.navNode` | Attributes `NavId` and `Links` (comma-separated ids) |
| `BK.dismountPad` | Model named after the id, tagged `DismountPad`, attributes `PadId`, `Radius`, `Center`. Children: `Ring`, `Disc`, `Label` (floor text made from the id), `EdgeLight1..4`, `ExitPoint`. The visuals never collide |
| `BK.barrier` | Stays queryable (lunge pre-checks), tagged `NoCollideCamera` |

## 4. Hierarchy and naming

```
Workspace
  Map
    CentralCommand
      OpsHall / Quarters / Briefing / Equipment / Medical / EastCorridor / WestCorridor
      Arrival / ObservationDeck / Research / Exterior / TrainingYard
        Structure   -- walls, floors, ceilings, stairs
        Detail      -- seams, trims, greebles (Detail tag)
        Props
        Lighting    -- fixture parts with lights
        Gameplay    -- Triggers, Prompts, Pads, Spawns, CamPoints, NavNodes, Barriers
    Hangar
      Shell / Bays / Catwalks / Crane / Door / LaunchPlatform / Causeway / Props / Lighting / Gameplay
    Backdrops
      City / Bulwark / Wilderness
    Outpost07
      Road / Perimeter / Courtyard / Bunker / PowerStation / MaintenanceYard
      Residential / Tower / Trail / Basin / Ridge / Bounds
    MemorySet
  Runtime            -- created by the server at runtime: Frames, Titans, NPCs, Effects
```
- Names: PascalCase, descriptive, unique within the parent (`Bay2_AccessBridge`, `Console_C3`, `Light_HighBay_R2_C4`).
- One **Model** per prop instance, with `PrimaryPart` set (or a pivot) so it can be moved as a unit.

## 5. Physics, collision, performance rules

- **All map geometry is Anchored.** Moving map parts (doors, crane, lever, rover roof) are anchored and moved by CFrame tweens: on the **server** if gameplay depends on them (doors, lever), on the **client** if purely ambient (crane, forklift, beacons, tag `AmbientMover`).
- **Collision groups** (created at server start by `CollisionService`):

| Group | Collides with |
|---|---|
| `Default` (map) | everything except `NoCollide` |
| `Players` | Default, PlayerBarrier |
| `FrameRoot` (Frame HRPs) | Default, FrameBarrier |
| `TitanRoot` (Titan HRPs) | Default |
| `NPCs` | Default |
| `FrameBarrier` | FrameRoot only |
| `PlayerBarrier` | Players only |
| `Debris` | Default only |
| `NoCollide` | nothing |

  Players ↔ FrameRoot, Players ↔ TitanRoot, FrameRoot ↔ TitanRoot and NPCs ↔ Players **do not collide**. Frame/Titan separation is handled in code (`12_combat_system.md` §9).
- **Frame-scale blocking:** a Frame's HRP spans Y 22.4–38.4 (64-stud Frames, D-044; it was 14–24), so anything lower than 22 studs won't block it physically, **and a Frame walks up onto anything lower than itself that it isn't blocked by** (it stood on a 36-stud training dummy in play, D-049). Put an invisible `FrameBarrier` box over every building, vehicle cluster or prop group a Frame shouldn't walk through (height 40), and around mission bounds.
- **Budgets:**

| Area | Max parts | Max lights (any) | Max shadowed lights |
|---|---|---|---|
| Central Command (all areas, excl. hangar) | 9,000 | 220 | 24 per 150-stud radius |
| Hangar + launch + causeway | 6,000 | 90 | 20 |
| Backdrops (city, Bulwark, wilderness) | 2,500 | 60 (no shadows) | 0 |
| Outpost 07 + trail + basin + ridge | 12,000 | 160 | 24 per 150-stud radius |
| Vanguard (each) | 450 | 6 | 0 |
| Strider | 350 | 4 | 0 |
| Watcher | 380 | 6 | 0 |
| Human NPC (gear only) | 40 | 0 | 0 |
| **Total in Workspace at once** | **≤ 40,000** (target 30,000) | | |

- `CanQuery = false` on every detail part (keeps raycasts and spatial queries fast).
- No Unions unless a shape is impossible with wedges, cylinders and balls; log each union in `decisions.md`.
- Parts max 2048 studs per axis. Large ground is tiled at 512 × 512.
- **StreamingEnabled = false** for the Vertical Slice (decision: simpler and safe at these part counts). Re-evaluate in Phase 7 with measurements (`19_testing_and_debug.md` §6).

## 6. Props catalog (exact recipes)

Each prop is a function in `lib/Props/`: `Props.<Name>(parent, cframe, opts) -> Model` (PrimaryPart set). The CFrame is the prop's **bottom-center** on the floor, facing −Z: a prop's front is the side its user stands or sits at, or the side its screen or sign shows (`Props.FACE["+Z"]` turns a prop to face south). **Wall props** (Banner, Poster, Vent, a wall-mounted HoloPanel) take the center of their back on the wall surface, −Z pointing out of the wall. One-off room dressing (a rug, a shelf, a jacket on a hook) is built inline by the area's builder and isn't catalogued (D-100). Detail parts of a prop never collide, cast shadows or answer queries (a queryable detail in front of a prompt's part blocks the prompt's line of sight). Sizes in studs (W × H × D).

| Prop | Size | Recipe |
|---|---|---|
| **Crate** (S/M/L) | 3×3×3 / 4×4×4 / 6×4×4 | Body WoodPlanks `WOOD_OLD`; 4 vertical edge battens 0.3 wide `#4F3E2E`; 1 stencil SurfaceGui ("UDD", "HALDEN", "FRAGILE") on ±Z; M/L get 2 metal corner caps `STEEL_DARK` |
| **CrateStack** | varies | 3–6 crates, seeded rotation ±8°, top crate offset |
| **MetalCase** | 4×2×2.5 | Body Metal `STEEL_MID`, lid seam 0.1 dark, 2 clasps Neon `AMBER` tiny, handle bar |
| **Barrel** | Ø2.6 × 3.6 | Cylinder `#5B6770` or `RUST`; 2 rings 0.2 `STEEL_DARK`; lid disc |
| **ToolCart** | 4×3.2×2.5 | Frame `STEEL_DARK`, 3 shelves `HAZARD_YELLOW` (top) / `STEEL_MID`, 4 Ø0.8 wheels, 3–5 tool blocks on top (wrench = 2 parts, box = 1) |
| **Console** | 6×3×2.5 | Base `STEEL_DARK` (6×2.6×2.5); top slanted wedge `STEEL_MID`; screen Neon `#1B2A33` 4.6×1.6 at a 25° tilt with a SurfaceGui of 3 lines of amber text plus 1 bar graph; keyboard strip 3.8×0.15×0.6 `KICKPLATE`. As built (D-100): the tilt is read from the horizontal, so the slope wedge makes it 3.3 tall; the screen lies on the slope; 4 lamps on the ledge; `opts.holo` adds a small amber projection over the back |
| **Chair** | 2×3.6×2 | Seat `FABRIC_DARK`, back, 1 central post, 5-star base (5 thin parts) |
| **Bench** | 8×1.8×1.6 | Seat slab `FABRIC_DARK` over 2 legs `STEEL_DARK` |
| **Bunk** | 7×2×3.5 | Frame `STEEL_DARK`, mattress `FABRIC_DARK` 6.6×0.6×3.2, pillow `#B7BCC2`, folded blanket `#4A5A6A` |
| **Locker** (row of N) | 2×7×2 each | Body `SLATE`, door seam lines, vent slits (3 thin dark bars), name plate tiny white |
| **Desk** | 5×2.8×2.5 | Top `#5A5F66`, 2 side panels, drawer block |
| **Terminal** (desk-top) | 1.8×1.4×0.3 | Screen Neon `#1B2A33` with amber SurfaceGui; base stand |
| **Photo frame** | 0.8×1×0.1 | Frame `#3A2A1E`; "photo" = SurfaceGui text "9TH FDU — 2180" plus 5 simple silhouette blocks |
| **Bed (medical)** | 7×2.6×3.4 | Frame white `MEDICAL_WHITE`, mattress `#C9D2DA`, side rails, monitor on an arm with a Neon green line |
| **Scanner arch** | 7×9×2 | 2 pillars `MEDICAL_WHITE` plus top beam; inner Neon strip `LIGHT_COOL`; scan ring (Neon ring made of 16 small parts or 1 thin cylinder) that tweens down |
| **Holo-table** | Ø20 × 3.2 | Base cylinder `STEEL_DARK` Ø20 × 2.8; rim ring `AMBER` Neon 0.3 thick; top glass disc; hologram = 25–40 small transparent Neon `#FFD38A` parts (Transparency 0.6) forming terrain blocks plus a red blinking marker for Outpost 07 (client blink 1 Hz) |
| **FloodlightMast** | 2×50×2 | Lattice mast: 4 thin vertical bars plus diagonal braces every 6 studs (`STEEL_DARK`); head = 2 lamp boxes 3×2×2 with Neon faces `LIGHT_COOL` plus SpotLight (Brightness 3, Range 60 [the Roblox maximum], Angle 50, Shadows true for at most 4 masts per area) |
| **Jersey barrier** | 6×3×2 | Wedge-profile concrete (base box plus 2 wedges), `CONCRETE_LIGHT`, hazard band |
| **WallSegment (outpost)** | 20×18×4 | Concrete `CONCRETE_MID`; top coping 20×1×5 `CONCRETE_DARK`; 2 pilasters; razor wire = 2 thin cylinders along the top plus zigzag thin parts |
| **Sandbags** | 6×2.5×2 | 3 rows of rounded "bags" = cylinders lying along X (`#8A7B5E`), offset per row |

## 7. Detailing recipes (apply in the `dressed` pass)

- **Wall panel seams:** vertical seams every 16 studs, horizontal at 3 (wainscot top) and 10. Width 0.2, inset 0.05 proud, color 8% darker than the wall.
- **Pilasters:** 2 × wallHeight × 1 every 24 studs on long exterior walls, `CONCRETE_DARK`, with a 1-stud chamfer wedge on top.
- **Pipes:** at least one pipe run along every industrial ceiling (hangar, corridors near the hangar, the outpost bunker).
- **Grime:** a 0.1-thick strip (`#2E3236`, transparency 0.6) beneath every vent and window, 2 studs long.
- **Cable sag:** between poles, 6 segments, sag = 4% of span.
- **Greebles on machines:** small boxes, cylinders and pipes (0.3–1.5 studs), at 4–10 per 10×10 face on Frames and machinery. Never on Titans (Titans are organic: sinew strips and bone plates instead).

## 8. How Claude verifies a build

1. The builder's returned stats are within budget.
2. A **spec check** script (`builders/checks/<Area>Check.lua`) asserts: bounding box ≈ spec ± 1 stud; every required named object exists (doors, prompts, spawn points, triggers, pads, cam points); walkable route connectivity (raycast down along the nav nodes: every node has floor beneath, and every link is clear of colliding walls by a capsule cast of radius 1.5 at height 3).
3. Play-mode walk test with the debug teleport (`19_testing_and_debug.md`).
4. **Ask the user for screenshots** of key views at the end of each area's `structure` and `dressed` passes. Claude Code accepts pasted images, so compare them against the spec and fix what looks wrong.
